entities.summary:
Luigi Torchi (1858–1920) was an Italian musicologist and composer important in the late nineteenth-century revival of early Italian music. Through editions, essays, and advocacy he helped recover Renaissance and Baroque repertories for a culture that had long privileged contemporary opera over historical sacred and instrumental works.

Torchi’s scholarship participated in a wider European early-music awakening—parallel to German and French editorial projects—while serving Italian national pride in pre-operatic traditions. Publishing old scores made them available to choirs, historians, and curious performers before the later twentieth-century HIP movement.

He stands among the founding editors who built the documentary basis for Italy’s historical musical self-understanding beyond Verdi and Puccini.
